patch.source_text: The 1 km phase-entry and BSE surfaces are aggregated to the coarser precipitation grid. patch.source_text: From a Data-Fitness-For-Purpose (DFFP) perspective, three complementary quality dimensions are addressed: (1) the plausibility of the input VGI observations; (2) producer’s accuracy, quantified by train-test cross-validation metrics such as RMSE and MAE; and (3) spatially explicit uncertainty surfaces, complemented by a separate assessment of prediction-interval reliability (coverage) and width.

evidence_the-producer-workflow-performs-.reason: Claim verified; added composite Sect. 2.3/2.3.5 provenance and expanded the evidence text to explicitly support both spatial interpolation and the separate PICP/MPIW coverage-and-width assessment.

patch.source_text: The function spatial_interpolation() maps the optimal station-level DOY predictions to the full 1 km grid of Germany using one of three methods. Prediction-interval coverage is evaluated separately from the production BSE using five-fold cross-validation. Prediction-interval coverage probability (PICP) describes empirical coverage, while mean prediction-interval width (MPIW) describes mean interval width.

patch.source_text: The workflow ingests point-scale phenological observations provided by the German Meteorological Service (Deutscher Wetterdienst, DWD) and combines them with gridded daily mean temperatures and a digital elevation model (DEM) to produce time series of interpolated DOY grids for eight main agricultural crop types and their associated phenological phases.

patch.source_section: 1 Introduction; 2.4 Data publication and FAIR packaging
patch.source_text: The dataset is extended annually as soon as the DWD has released the quality-checked observations of the completed vegetation period. Since PhenoPhaseR version 1.2, publication is not a separate manual step but an integral part of each processing run; two publish hooks are executed at the end of the pipeline.

evidence_validation-and-uncertainty-depe.reason: Claim verified; narrowed the provenance to limitations 1 and 5, which explicitly support station-density/spatial-support sensitivity and the aggregation-scale limitation.

patch.source_text: Station density varies considerably over space and time, and predictions in sparsely observed regions should be treated with greater caution, particularly where they extend beyond the main support of the observation network. The validation and the PICP/MPIW assessment are based on phenological observation locations and therefore assess model performance where observations are available, not across all cells of the Germany-wide prediction grid. In the weather-indicator uncertainty propagation, aggregation of the 1 km BSE to the coarser E-OBS grid does not explicitly account for spatial covariance.
